SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which direction lies between south and east? (1 mark)
   A. North-east
   B. South-east
   C. South-west
   D. North-west

2. Which direction lies between north and west? (1 mark)
   A. North-west
   B. South-east
   C. North-east
   D. South-west

3. On the county map in the lesson, the neighbour drawn on the right side is in which direction from the county? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. South
   C. East
   D. North

4. Which ocean is found on the south-eastern side of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Atlantic Ocean
   B. Pacific Ocean
   C. Indian Ocean
   D. Arctic Ocean

5. What is a plateau? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A coast
   C. High land that is flat on top
   D. A deep valley

6. What is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   B. A market
   C. A road
   D. A building made by people

7. Which of these actions harms a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Sweeping the compound
   B. Picking up litter
   C. Writing on the walls
   D. Learning its story

8. What is the difference between a museum and a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A cultural centre has no dances
   B. A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   C. A museum is always outdoors
   D. There is no difference

9. Which of these shows interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. A man refusing help
   B. Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   C. A woman sleeping
   D. A child eating alone

10. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a nurse give? (1 mark)
   A. Learning
   B. Transport
   C. Food
   D. Health care

11. Which type of area in Kenya usually has few people for its size? (1 mark)
   A. Big cities
   B. Dry areas in the far north
   C. Highlands around Mount Kenya
   D. Busy lakeshores

12. Which is a reason why fewer people live in a forest reserve? (1 mark)
   A. It has many towns
   B. There are too many houses
   C. It has good roads
   D. People are not allowed to settle there

13. In a bar graph of sub-county populations, which sub-county has the tallest bar? (1 mark)
   A. The one with the most people
   B. The largest area
   C. The smallest area
   D. The one with the fewest people

14. What do we call an area where few people live in a large space? (1 mark)
   A. Busy
   B. Crowded
   C. Sparsely populated
   D. Densely populated

15. Which of these is a Maasai red or blue checked cloth? (1 mark)
   A. Shuka
   B. Uniform
   C. Kanga
   D. Kikoi

16. Which is a way of conserving forests? (1 mark)
   A. Planting more trees than we cut
   B. Building fires
   C. Burning the forest
   D. Cutting all trees

17. What is one problem that industries can cause? (1 mark)
   A. Pollution
   B. Fewer jobs
   C. Less trade
   D. More rain

18. Which is an agro-based industry? (1 mark)
   A. A hotel
   B. A school
   C. A bank
   D. A tea factory

19. Which of these helps drivers to see pupils on the road? (1 mark)
   A. A black bag
   B. A hat that covers the eyes
   C. Dark clothes
   D. Reflective strips

20. What is an enterprise? (1 mark)
   A. A business activity to make goods or provide services
   B. A game
   C. A weather chart
   D. A school rule

21. What is income? (1 mark)
   A. Money received from selling
   B. Money borrowed
   C. Money spent
   D. Money lost

22. Which information should you not share with strangers online? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. The name of your favourite fruit
   C. Your home address and password
   D. A joke

23. Which is a benefit of good citizenship in school? (1 mark)
   A. Less learning
   B. The school is safe and orderly
   C. More fights
   D. Property is broken

24. Which of these spoils peace? (1 mark)
   A. Fairness
   B. Bullying
   C. Listening
   D. Forgiveness

25. What is child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Playing with a child
   B. Feeding a child
   C. Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   D. Teaching a child

26. What are tally marks used for? (1 mark)
   A. Counting votes
   B. Cooking
   C. Painting
   D. Measuring rain

27. What is a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A kind of road
   C. A large family group with a common ancestor
   D. A market

28. Which duty belongs to a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. Leading prayers and teaching values
   B. Making laws
   C. Selling goods
   D. Repairing cars

29. Which law created county governments in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   B. A market rule
   C. A school rule
   D. A church rule

30. Which best describes the difference between the governor and an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor
   B. They do the same job
   C. An MCA is above the governor
   D. The governor makes laws

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give two reasons why farmers plant crops at the start of the rainy season. (2 marks)

32. What is a sub-county? (2 marks)

33. Explain the difference between a physical feature and a built feature. Give one example of each. (4 marks)

34. Give two reasons why we obey school rules. (2 marks)

35. Describe what you should do if you are being bullied. (3 marks)

36. List four factors a company thinks about before building a factory. (4 marks)

37. Explain how a county with a big lake and a dry plain could earn a living from both. (4 marks)

38. Explain how a village elder can help two neighbours who quarrel about a fence. (4 marks)

39. Give three qualities of a good leader and explain why each matters. (3 marks)

40. Draw a side view of the land showing a mountain, a valley and a plain and label them. (5 marks)

41. Describe how you would show a river, a lake and a mountain on a map with a key. (3 marks)

42. Describe how you would prepare for a class visit to a museum, and what you would do during the visit. (5 marks)

43. Explain why many factories are built near big towns. (3 marks)

44. Explain how good citizenship in school prepares pupils to be good citizens of Kenya. (4 marks)

45. Name the four cardinal points. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — South-east
   South-east is half way between south and east.

2. A — North-west
   North-west is between north and west.

3. C — East
   When north is at the top, the right side is east.

4. C — Indian Ocean
   Kenya's coast is on the Indian Ocean.

5. C — High land that is flat on top
   A plateau is a raised area with a flat top.

6. A — A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   Physical features such as mountains and rivers are natural.

7. C — Writing on the walls
   Writing on old walls spoils them.

8. B — A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
   Cultural centres let visitors see and take part in living culture.

9. B — Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
   The farmer and tailor depend on each other.

10. D — Health care
   Nurses give health care.

11. B — Dry areas in the far north
   Dry northern areas are sparsely populated.

12. D — People are not allowed to settle there
   Forest reserves are protected.

13. A — The one with the most people
   Taller bars show bigger values.

14. C — Sparsely populated
   Sparse means thinly spread.

15. A — Shuka
   The shuka is a checked cloth worn by the Maasai.

16. A — Planting more trees than we cut
   Replanting keeps the forest alive.

17. A — Pollution
   Waste from factories can pollute air and water.

18. D — A tea factory
   Agro-based industries use farm produce.

19. D — Reflective strips
   Reflective strips shine in light.

20. A — A business activity to make goods or provide services
   Enterprises earn money by making goods or services.

21. A — Money received from selling
   Income is what you receive from sales.

22. C — Your home address and password
   Private details must be kept safe.

23. B — The school is safe and orderly
   Good citizens make a peaceful school.

24. B — Bullying
   Bullying hurts and frightens people.

25. C — Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   Abuse harms a child's body, feelings or future.

26. A — Counting votes
   Tally marks help count votes.

27. C — A large family group with a common ancestor
   A clan traces its origin to one ancestor.

28. A — Leading prayers and teaching values
   Religious leaders lead worship.

29. A — The Constitution of Kenya 2010
   The 2010 Constitution created counties.

30. A — The governor runs the county; an MCA makes laws and checks the governor
   They have different roles.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rain gives the seeds water to grow, and the wet soil is soft to dig.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sub-county is a smaller part of a county. Each county is divided into sub-counties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it is a smaller part, 1 mark for the link with a county.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: A physical feature is natural, such as a mountain. A built feature is made by people, such as a bridge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct example.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rules keep everyone safe and they help everyone to learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stay calm and do not fight back, walk away to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Raw materials, market, transport, and water and power. Accept workers or land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: People can fish in the lake and sell the fish. People on the dry plain can keep cattle and goats. Both bring food and income. The county can also use both for tourism.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to both, be fair, help them to talk and agree, and encourage them to forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty so people trust the leader, fairness so all are treated equally, and listening so decisions are wise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with reason.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with a high peak labelled mountain, a low dip labelled valley and a flat area labelled plain.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape drawn and 1 mark for each label, up to 5 marks.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wavy blue line for a river, a blue patch for a lake and a brown triangle or brown shading for a mountain, with a key that explains them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct symbol described, up to 3.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission from the teacher and the museum, prepare questions, take a notebook, stay with the group, listen to the guide, take notes and do not touch objects.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 5.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Many customers live there. Workers live nearby. Roads and other services are available.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Pupils learn to follow rules, respect others, take care of public property and take responsibility. These habits continue when they are adults.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: North, east, south and west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct points, 2 marks for all four.
